value.signature: fn verifier (salt : Input < '_ > , stored_key : Input < '_ > , server_key : Input < '_ > , output : Output < '_ >) -> Result < () , Error >

review.body: { if salt . 0 . len () != SALT_LENGTH || stored_key . 0 . len () != KEY_LENGTH || server_key . 0 . len () != KEY_LENGTH || output . 0 . len () != VERIFIER_LENGTH { return Err (Error :: Bound) ; } output . 0 [.. 21] . copy_from_slice (b"SCRAM-SHA-256$600000:") ; STANDARD . encode_slice (salt . 0 , & mut output . 0 [21 .. 45]) . map_err (| _ | Error :: Primitive) ? ; output . 0 [45] = b'$' ; STANDARD . encode_slice (stored_key . 0 , & mut output . 0 [46 .. 90]) . map_err (| _ | Error :: Primitive) ? ; output . 0 [90] = b':' ; STANDARD . encode_slice (server_key . 0 , & mut output . 0 [91 ..]) . map_err (| _ | Error :: Primitive) ? ; Ok (()) }
review.item_premise: The borrowed operations write only caller-owned destinations, Error has no payload, and no result contains private bytes. Inputs remain protected by their caller. The verifier formatter has no admitted production consumer. Its borrows and primitive temporaries, including encoder copies of stored-key and server-key bytes, are owed to its first consumer's inventory review; no host residue disposition is inherited.
